expect: the PLGA/PLA/PCL polymer system (~180 nm), sEVs (~150 nm), MOF@EVs (~168 nm) and MOF (~485 nm, the largest); passive targeting covers the rows down to GO (active targeting)
question: In Table 2, which passive-targeting delivery systems have a particle size of 150 nm or more, and which of them is the largest?
rendered:
From Table 2, the passive-targeting delivery systems with a particle size of 150 nm or more are:

- sEVs | – | VEGFR2 siRNA mTOR | VEGFR2 | ~150 nm
- US-EV | – | HMME siYTHDF1 | YTHDF1 | 139.83 nm (less than 150 nm)
- MOF@EVs | – | siTEAD4 | TEAD4 | ~168 nm
- AuNP | PEG-SH | TUBB2B siRNA- AuNP | TUBB2B | – (no particle size provided)
- SPIONs | PEN | siSnail2 | Snail2 | ~60 nm (less than 150 nm)
- MOF | – | DDP | VEGF | ~485 nm
- MOF | – | siVEGF | siVEGF: Release is accelerated under acidic conditions

The largest particle size among these is ~485 nm, which is the particle size of the MOF delivery system targeting VEGF.
